messages:
michael: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection heuristic change, we're seeing a noticeable bump in tail latency and a few OOMs on the p4d dedicated pool. repro traces attached.

anya: ugh. can you paste the profiler top-lines here?

michael: sure, quick excerpt from the device allocator profiler: 
```
2026-03-11T14:02:03Z peak_gpu_mem=48.3GB total_gpu=80GB
alloc_calls/s=1200 alloc_bytes/s=1.9GB
active_kv_cache=9.8GB (growing with long-history requests)
scratchpad_peak=6.2GB (per-kernel workspace spikes)
logits_ephemeral=1.6GB (many small allocations)
activation_churn=850 allocs/s for activations
fragmentation_ratio=0.22
```

raj: the scratchpad and logits allocations look like the main churn sources. kernel-selection change likely chose kernels with larger workspace needs for some seqLen/profile combos.

sofia: also noticed worst-case when batching heuristic packs mixed short+long sequences into the same batch — that increases workspace requirements.

kevin: +1. mixing lifetimes kills reuse. current allocator is cudaMalloc-free + simple free list, so we get lots of small heat allocations and fragmentation.

michael: proposal: implement a device-local tensor pool with size-classes and three logical pools: activations, logits, scratchpads. reuse by lifetime class and allow quick memzero. keep eviction LRU for idle buffers. this should reduce alloc churn and fragmentation.

anya: sounds good. couple of questions:
- how do we handle KV cache which grows across tokens and has very different lifetime?
- what about kernels that sometimes need much bigger workspace than others (peak spikes)?

raj: ideas:
- KV cache stays in a separate reserved pool that is only grown but can be opportunistically trimmed by evicting cold entries + persist to host if needed.
- scratchpad pool should support "temp-resize" semantics: if a kernel requests larger than max-class, allocate an ephemeral buffer (tracked) and record a metric; if ephemeral allocs > threshold, bump a device-level large-class size for subsequent runs.

sofia: also add an OOM mitigation path: on OOM, try: 1) drop small-prefetched KV entries, 2) fall back to a cheaper kernel with smaller workspace, 3) retry with smaller batch or split batch, 4) spill scratchpad to host pinned memory (last resort).

kevin: implementation notes:
- size classes powers-of-two up to 32MB by default, with ability to configure per-model.
- keep a ring/pool per size-class and per-buffer-type to avoid cross-type reuse issues.
- record per-alloc histograms to auto-tune class boundaries.

michael: profiling plan: add counters for alloc latency, ephemeral alloc rate, fragmentation ratio, pool hit rate, and per-kernel workspace requests. run canaries on a dedicated small fleet (p4d-small) for 72h synthetic + real traffic.

anya: perf regression concern — pooling reduces alloc overhead but may increase peak resident memory if we overprovision classes. we should set defaults conservative and enable auto-shrink for idle buffers after N secs.

raj: agree. also add a safety threshold that keeps X% headroom (configurable) and triggers eager eviction behavior before reaching it.

sofia: can we do a non-invasive canary: enable pooling only for scratchpads/logits first (not activations nor KV cache) and observe tail latency & OOM rate?

michael: yes. rollout plan:
- stage 1 (canary): scratchpad + logits pooling, ephemeral fallback, metrics (2 days) — owner: michael
- stage 2: add auto-tuning size-classes + idle shrink, run A/B with current allocator (3 days) — owner: kevin
- stage 3: activation pooling + KV reserved pool + OOM mitigation + canary across more regions (1 week) — owner: raj

kevin: test harness to run: synthetic varied seqLen mixes, long KV-history replay, and real traffic shadowing. need infra assistance to provision canary nodes.

infra-bot: @eng-runtime created canary cluster request #CANARY-435 for 6 p4d-small nodes in us-west-2. ETA provisioning 2h.

anya: awesome. mike/kevin/raj — please post the lightweight runbook for the rollback steps in the canary thread. also include metrics thresholds to auto-disable pooling if error rate or tail latency regresses >5%.

michael: will do. quick follow-ups after the first run: if pool hit-rate < 80% or fragmentation ratio increases, we revert and profile further. otherwise we promote to more nodes. :thumbsup:

kevin: adding a small perf note: kernel selection heuristics should be made aware of current pool sizes / workspace availability. scheduler could prefer kernels with smaller workspace when memory headroom is low.

michael: good call. adding kernel-aware routing to the list.

sofia: thanks everyone. capturing action items in the ticket.

michael: (closing) will update thread when canary metrics are in.
